name: The Hartford Insurance Group, Inc.
base_source: TTM core earnings per share: FY2025 $13.42 - H1 2025 $5.44 (Q1 $2.20 + Q2 $3.24) + H1 2026 $6.51 (Q1 $3.09 + Q2 $3.42) = $14.49. Engine OCF base rejected for an insurer: 3-yr median $19.30/share, TTM OCF ~$20.61/share (FY OCF $5,922M - H1'25 $2,276M + H1'26 $2,234M = $5,880M, capex TTM $7M, SBC ~$141M, / 278.1M shares) capitalizes float/reserve growth, not distributable earnings. See analysis.md.
moat_justification: Leading small-commercial/workers' comp specialization, exclusive decades-long AARP personal-lines distribution, top-tier Employee Benefits scale, high-80s underlying combined ratios and 18.7-20.3% core ROE — against price-competed commodity P&C products with no structural pricing power, rising CAT exposure, recurring legacy long-tail reserve charges (A&E, sexual-abuse), and earnings partly hostage to investment/LP marks.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.5x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 4.6%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Finance sector — OE/capex DCF fits banks/insurers poorly; grade confidence low
one_liner: High-quality P&C / employee-benefits insurer, moat 5/10 — engine OCF base is an insurer float artifact (preliminary Tier A rejected); on TTM core earnings of $14.49/share the $131.14 price (9.0x core, 1.66x BV ex-AOCI) yields a 17.1% weighted IRR, IV@15% $154.75 — clears 15% at ~$155, ~$124 with a margin of safety, confidence low (sector mismatch).
